title: SIGNN++: Robust Graph Neural Star Identification on Earth
abstract: arXiv:2610.30186v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: We present SIGNN++, a learning-based star identification (SID) framework for celestial navigation in GNSS-denied nighttime environments. Although researchers have developed learning-based SID methods to improve robustness to observation noise, prior evaluations have focused mainly on synthetic or non-terrestrial environments, leaving their reliability under real terrestrial conditions unclear. To address these limitations, SIGNN++ extends SIGNN, a graph neural network-based SID method, with three components: a more realistic noise model for training data, Fourier Transform (FT) of angular-distance edge features, and RANSAC-based Perspective Star Alignment for identification and attitude refinement. The results show that SIGNN++ is more robust to terrestrial observation disturbances and achieves higher star identification accuracy and solved rates than the original SIGNN and publicly available SID baselines, while maintaining comparable

tldr: SIGNN++通过更真实的训练噪声模型、角距边特征的傅里叶变换以及基于RANSAC的透视星对齐三项改进，显著提升了图神经网络星图识别方法在真实地面观测环境下的鲁棒性、识别精度与求解率。
en_tdlr: SIGNN++ improves the robustness, accuracy, and solved rates of graph neural network-based star identification under real terrestrial observation conditions through a more realistic noise model, Fourier transform of angular-distance edge features, and RANSAC-based perspective star alignment.
